headline: On November 20, 1998: Zarya launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome
captionCards: Still serves as a critical storage module on the ISS today
instagramCaption:
Zarya lifted off on November 20, 1998, from Kazakhstan's Baikonur Cosmodrome.

The first ISS module, built in Russia but funded by the U.S., was launched atop a Proton-K rocket.
It provided power, propulsion, and guidance during the station’s early years.
Its name, meaning 'sunrise,' symbolized a new era of international space cooperation.
Today, it remains a key storage module on the ISS.
